 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioner is before this Court seeking his enlargement on bail for it having been turned down by the learned Sessions Judge in terms of its order dated 05.01.2023 in Spl. S.C POCSO No.68/2022.
2.
Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader.

3. Facts in brief are as follows:
A crime comes to be registered on 27.10.2022 in Crime No.283/2022 initially for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC.
This was based upon a complaint by the complainant that his daughter/ victim went missing from 01:30 p.m on 23.10.2022.
Later, the daughter was traced and it was noticed that, the petitioner has indulged in physical relationship with the daughter.
At the relevant point in time the daughter was aged 17 years 11 months and 19 days therefore she was 11 days short to become 18 years.
Therefore the offences alleged are the one punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012, inter alia.
The petitioner since 01.11.2022 has been in custody.

The police after investigation have filed a charge sheet against the petitioner for offences punishable under Sections 363 and 376 of the IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act,
2012.
After filing the charge sheet the petitioner seeks his enlargement of bail which comes to be turned down in terms of the order dated 06.01.2023.
It is the denial of bail to the petitioner that drives the petitioner to this Court in the subject petition.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner and the respondent/ victim girl were in love and the acts were consensual.

The learned counsel further submits that the 164 statement rendered by the victim clearly states that she was in love with the accused and went along with him voluntarily and there was no allegation about the sexual intercourse.

sentences.text: 5. The learned High Court Government Pleader would however seeks dismissal of the petition on the ground that the offences involved the offences are once punishable for rape and POCSO.
Therefore bail not to be granted.
6. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the respective learned counsel and perused the material on record.
7. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.

The petitioner was taken to custody on 01.11.2022 after the victim was found with him on a missing complaint filed by the complainant and offences punishable under Section 376 and 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 were laid against the petitioner.

8. A perusal of 164 statement of the victim that would clearly indicate that the victim girl voluntarily goes to the petitioner on the ground that she was in love with him and further states that they had no physical relationship with each other.
The age of the victim as on the date of the commission of the offence i.e., 22.10.2022 is 17 years 11 months and 19 days short of 11 days to become 18 years.

Therefore looking at the totality of the circumstances and the statement of the victim under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, I deem it appropriate to enlarge the petitioner on bail since he is in custody from 01.11.2022.
9.

For the aforesaid reason, the following:
ORDER The criminal petition is allowed.

The petitioner shall be released on bail in connection with Spl. SC. POCSO No.68/2022 pending on the file of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-1, Koppal, subject to the following conditions:
(i) The petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees two lakhs only) with one surety for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
